newsitem.title: CHINA: China snowstorms kill 34, more missing.
newsitem.headline: China snowstorms kill 34, more missing.

text.p: The fiercest snowstorms in 30 years have blanketed parts of China's far-west Xinjiang region, killing 34 people and nearly a million sheep and cutting off 100,000 residents, officials said on Wednesday.

Snowstorms that have raged for about a month in Xinjiang's Altay mountains on the border with Mongolia have sent temperatures plummeting to minus 36 degrees Celsius (minus 32 Fahrenheit), officials of the Ministry of Civil Affairs said. More snow was expected.
At least 34 people had died, most of them herders. The dead included two gold miners who froze to death, while four people were missing and 18 suffered severe frostbite.

The freezing temperatures and heavy snows that have caused the collapse of houses in some areas have killed at least 987,000 head of livestock, mostly sheep, in Altay as well as in Yili and Bayinggulu districts, officials said.
Up to 5,000 families living in the Altay mountains were without food and more than 30,000 people were short of food, official reports said.
More than 100,000 herders had been trapped by the snow in one part of the Altay region and some 980 gold miners had been stranded.

People's Liberation Army soldiers had found 25 geological surveyors who had been cut off for nearly 10 days by the storms, the Xinhua news agency said. The military had air-dropped food and medicines, as well as a radio, generators and other aid to the marooned surveyors.
The storms had dumped more than three times the usual snowfall in many areas while in the worst-hit areas the snow was up to six or nine times the average, the ministry said.
Earlier reports said the snow was more than two metres (yards) deep in many places.
The ministry estimated economic losses so far at 247 million yuan ($29 million) and earlier reports said the government had allocated more than 25 million yuan ($3 million) for disaster relief.
Further snowfalls were expected, the ministry said.
Many residents of the sparsely-populated region are nomads who raise cattle, goats or sheep for a living.
